meta.title: Global Crude Flow Intelligence Dashboard
meta.week_convention: Weeks run Monday-Sunday; week_ending is always the Sunday, with data captured up to the 09:00 Europe/Nicosia (Cyprus time) cutoff that Sunday morning.
meta.note: Built from free/public sources (EIA, IEA, OPEC, operator statements, Reuters/Al Jazeera/Bloomberg/OilPrice/Argus/Kpler-cited reporting) plus a seed route database. No live Kpler/Vortexa feed is connected in this build; flow figures are research snapshots, not real-time AIS-derived data. See each item's confidence tag and source.

disruptions.description: "2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis": US/Israel strikes on Iran (Operation Epic Fury, 28 Feb 2026) triggered Iranian closure of the strait, ship boardings and mining. Ceasefire (8 Apr) failed; US naval blockade of Iranian ports (13 Apr-29 May); further escalation 5-6 Sept 2026 (US struck 3 Iranian tankers, Iran fired missiles at US warships). Brent spiked to $126 in March, back to $96.28 on 6 Sept 2026. Saudi Arabia (-20%), Iraq (-70% at peak), Kuwait, Qatar, UAE and Iran all hit. Bypass routes (Saudi East-West/Yanbu, UAE Habshan-Fujairah, Iraq Kirkuk-Ceyhan) together carry only ~9 mb/d vs the ~20 mb/d the strait normally carries.
disruptions.source: Wikipedia: 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis; Al Jazeera (6-7 Sep 2026)

disruptions.estimated_capacity_affected: Refining outlook cut to ~4 mb/d over next 18 months (-30% vs pre-invasion)
disruptions.actual_flow_affected: 2026 crude supply forecast cut by 125 kb/d to 8.7 mb/d
disruptions.expected_restart: Repairs of secondary units estimated 6-8 months each
disruptions.description: IEA September 2026 monthly report: at least 22 Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian refineries in August 2026 alone, the highest monthly total of the war. Sanctions restrict replacement parts; Russia has extended bans on diesel/gasoline/jet fuel exports with regional fuel rationing in places.
disruptions.source: IEA monthly report via Rigzone (11 Sep 2026)

disruptions.description: Ukrainian drone attack ignited a fire at Ust-Luga, Russia’s largest Baltic export terminal, on 1 Sept 2026 (52 drones intercepted by air defence over 4 hours; fire out by ~09:30 Moscow time). Second strike on this terminal in three weeks (previous: 14 Aug 2026). Source article does not confirm whether/when normal loading resumed.
Marine industry reporting indicates Primorsk remained closed after drone attacks even as Ust-Luga briefly restarted oil exports; exact reopening date not confirmed in source.

Despite a Ukrainian drone strike on Novorossiysk port on 8 Apr 2026, Kazakhstan’s energy ministry confirmed CPC loadings continued normally. Ukraine agreed with the US (reported 8 Aug 2026) to refrain from targeting CPC-linked tankers specifically, reducing risk to this route relative to Russia’s own Baltic terminals.
disruptions.source: Ukrainska Pravda (8 Aug 2026); Pipeline Technology Journal
